question.worked_solution:
We need to isolate all terms with $c$ on one side of the equation. To do this, we start by subtracting $5$ from both sides: 

$$
\begin{aligned}4c+5 & =3yc-2 \\ 4c+5-5 & =3yc-2-5 \\ 4c & =3yc-7\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we subtract $3yc$ from both sides of the equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}4c & =3yc-7 \\ 4c-3yc & =3yc-7-3yc \\ 4c-3yc & =-7\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that all terms containing $c$ are on the left-hand side, and all terms independent of $c$ are on the right-hand side.

Next, we factor out $c$ in the expression on the left-hand side.

$$
\begin{aligned}4c-3yc & =-7 \\ c(4-3y) & =-7\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we divide both sides by $(4-3y)$ to isolate $c:$

$$
\begin{aligned}c(4-3y) & =-7 \\ \frac{c(4-3y)}{4-3y} & =\frac{-7}{4-3y} \\ \frac{c\cancel{(4-3y)}}{\cancel{4-3y}} & =-\frac{7}{4-3y} \\ c & =\frac{7}{3y-4}\end{aligned}
$$

**Note:** This result assumes that $3y-4\ne 0.$
